newsitem.title: USA: SGL class-action suit to take years - U.S. lawyer.
newsitem.headline: SGL class-action suit to take years - U.S. lawyer.

text.p: A lawyer pressing a U.S. class-action lawsuit alleging price-fixing by SGL Carbon AG on Wednesday said extensive infighting by attorneys was likely and a trial was probably years away.

Attorneys for SGL and two other producers of graphite electrodes named in the suit, UCAR International and Carbide/Graphite Group, have 45 days to respond to requests for information and executive interviews, according to David Manogue, the lawyer who filed the lawsuit.
"I do expect they will place roadblocks in the way," Manogue said.

According to the lawsuit, filed in U.S. District Court in Pittsburgh, the three companies cooperated illegally for the last five years to raise prices for graphite electrodes and cheated as many as 1,000 or more U.S. steelmakers by denying true price competition.

"The charged combination and conspiracy consisted of a continuing agreement, understanding and concert to action among defendants ... to raise, fix and maintain prices of graphite electrodes throughout the United States," the lawsuit said.

The lawsuit puts no amount on the alleged damages, but Manogue said the defendants would be assessed triple actual damages if found liable after a jury trial. He declined to discuss the likely level of such damages.

The lawsuit said the three companies accounted for 55 percent of the U.S. market for the electrodes, which analysts have said sell for less than they did in the 1980s. The electrodes are used in manufacturing steel.
"We don't know of any wrongdoing at all," said Peter Mancino, general counsel for UCAR. "We will vigorously oppose it."

Mancino said he believed the lawsuit, filed on behalf of Erie Forge and Steel Inc of Erie, Pennsylvania, and other steelmakers, was spurred by government investigations in both the United States and in Europe.

U.S. officials three weeks ago searched SGL Carbon's offices in Charlotte, North Carolina, and took away documents. German officials, aiding European Union investigators in Brussels, have searched offices of SGL and other other manufacturers.
SGL has denied it has done any wrongdoing and described the class-action suit as without merit.

Manogue said his law firm, Specter Law Offices of Pittsburgh, has filed many class-action suits in U.S. courts, including one against providers of molybdenum products to U.S. steelmakers. That suit, he said, was settled last autumn before trial for more than $6 million.
